headings.title: Prohibited wage-reducing subsidies, bid supplements, and rebates
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2007 S.B. 339, A.L. 2018 H.B. 1729, et al.). Prohibits contractors and subcontractors from directly or indirectly receiving a wage subsidy, bid supplement, or rebate for public works employment only if it reduces the employer's wage rate on an occupational title below the rate required under §§ 290.210 to 290.340.

headings.title: Reporting lawful subsidies, supplements, rebates, and public records
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 2007 S.B. 339, A.L. 2018 H.B. 1729, et al.). Requires an entity lawfully receiving a subsidy, supplement, or rebate under subsection 1 to report the date and amount to the public body within thirty days of payment receipt, and makes the disclosure report a public record under chapter 610.

headings.title: Liability for violations and department calculation duty
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note (L. 2007 S.B. 339, A.L. 2018 H.B. 1729, et al.). Provides that a violating employer owes the public body double the hourly wage reduction below §§ 290.210 to 290.340 rates for each hour worked, and assigns the department the duty to calculate the dollar amount owed.

headings.title: Requested corporate service letters and required contents
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and all source notes (RSMo 1939 § 5064, A.L. 1941 p. 330, A.L. 1982 S.B. 747; prior revisions 1929–1909; cross-reference to § 516.140; eight 1985–1990 case annotations, retaining verbatim source typo '1986)' missing opening parenthesis on Gloria v. University of Health Sciences). Covers qualified service-letter requests by certified mail referencing the statute within a reasonable period up to one year after discharge or voluntary quit from a corporation doing business in Missouri with seven or more employees after at least ninety days of service, and the superintendent's or manager's duty to issue a signed letter within forty-five days.

headings.title: Compensatory, nominal, and punitive damages limits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and all source notes (including § 516.140 cross-reference and 1985–1990 case annotations regarding actual, nominal, and punitive damages and malice). Provides corporate liability for compensatory but not punitive damages for subsection 1 violations, permits nominal and punitive damages if evidence establishes failure to issue the requested letter, and bars punitive damages based on letter content.

headings.title: Definitions of employer and prospective employer
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, subdivisions (1)–(2), and history note (L. 1999 S.B. 32). Defines 'employer' and 'prospective employer' for purposes of section 290.152.

headings.title: Permitted written disclosures to prospective employers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2, subdivisions (1)–(3) including continuation sentences in subdivision (3), and history note (L. 1999 S.B. 32). Authorizes an employer to respond in writing to a written request from a reasonably believed prospective employer disclosing service nature, character, duration, and true cause of discharge or quit, applicable even if hired before receipt and required to be consistent with any § 290.140 service letter.

headings.title: Sending and requesting copies of employer letters
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note (L. 1999 S.B. 32). Requires the employer to send a copy of any subsection 2 letter to the current or former employee's last known address, and allows the employee to request a copy for up to one year after the letter's date.

headings.title: Employer civil immunity and falsity exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note (L. 1999 S.B. 32). Grants an employer civil immunity for responses made under section 290.152 and their consequences, subject to an exception for false responses made with knowledge of falsity or reckless disregard for truth.

headings.title: Compensatory damages limit for subsection 2 violations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note (L. 1999 S.B. 32). Makes an employer who violates subsection 2 liable for compensatory damages but not punitive damages.

headings.title: Inadmissibility of letters in unemployment claims
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note (L. 1999 S.B. 32). Prohibits admission of any letter issued under section 290.152 as evidence in an unemployment compensation claim.

headings.title: Wage rates, Sunday-holiday pay, overtime, and lunch rules
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, subdivisions (1)–(4), including the continuation div block under subdivision (2)(g) on Monday observance of Sunday holidays, and history note (L. 1957 p. 574 § 3, A.L. 2014 H.B. 1594, A.L. 2018 H.B. 1729, et al.). Covers prevailing hourly or public works contracting minimum wage rates (excluding maintenance work), double rates for Sundays and seven listed holidays, one-and-one-half overtime rates (exceeding ten hours per day and forty hours per calendar week, excluding maintenance work or contractual obligation), and an unpaid thirty-minute daily lunch period.

headings.title: On-site construction workers deemed employed on public works
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1957 p. 574 § 3, as amended through A.L. 2018 H.B. 1729, et al.). Limits those deemed employed upon public works to workers directly employed by contractors or subcontractors in actual construction work on the site of the building or construction job.

headings.title: Unpaid volunteer labor exception and anti-coercion rule
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note (A.L. 2014 H.B. 1594, A.L. 2018 H.B. 1729, et al.). Excludes workers who agree in writing to volunteer labor without pay from §§ 290.210 to 290.340 wage entitlements, defines qualifying volunteers (excluding prisoners, criminal community-service workers, and workers compensated on the same project), and prohibits employers or public bodies from forcing, compelling, or intimidating workers to volunteer.

headings.title: Dual-capacity hauling and construction workers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note (L. 1957 p. 574 § 3, as amended through A.L. 2018 H.B. 1729, et al.). Provides that workers whose hauling of materials or equipment includes a phase of construction beyond mere transportation to the site are deemed employed directly on public works.

headings.title: Seventy-five-thousand-dollar project threshold and cost calculation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5, subdivisions (1)–(3), and history note (A.L. 2018 H.B. 1729, et al.). Exempts public works construction whose engineer's estimate or accepted bid for total project cost is $75,000 or less from §§ 290.210 to 290.340, bases cost on the entire project rather than sub-projects, and includes all contractor/subcontractor labor value plus purchased materials and supplies.

headings.title: Prohibition on dividing projects to avoid threshold
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note (A.L. 2018 H.B. 1729, et al.). Prohibits a public body from dividing a project into multiple contracts to lower total project cost below the subsection 5 threshold.

headings.title: Change orders pushing project cost above threshold
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note (A.L. 2018 H.B. 1729, et al.). Provides that if an initially $75,000-or-less public works project exceeds $75,000 due to a change order, §§ 290.210 to 290.340 apply only to the portion in excess of $75,000.

headings.title: Competitive-bidding exemption at or below ten thousand dollars
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history note (A.L. 2018 H.B. 1729, et al.). Exempts public bodies from competitive-bidding laws for public works construction whose engineer's estimate or accepted bid for total project cost is $10,000 or less for all occupational titles.

headings.title: On-the-job training workers and fifty-percent wage rate

headings.title: One-to-one ratio limit with journeyman workers

Caps the combined total of entry-level workers and federally registered apprentices at a one-to-one ratio with journeyman workers in any occupational title on a public works project subject to §§ 290.210 to 290.340.

headings.title: Department rulemaking authority under sections 290.210 to 290.340
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1957 p. 574 § 6, as amended through A.L. 2018 H.B. 1729, et al.). Authorizes the department to establish rules and regulations to carry out §§ 290.210 to 290.340.

headings.title: Complaint investigations, violation findings, and penalty notices
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (A.L. 2007 S.B. 339, A.L. 2018 H.B. 1729, et al.). Requires the department to investigate complaints by § 290.240 interested parties, notify the employer of findings, issue a notice of penalty if a violation and potential penalty are found, and defer penalty due date until forty-five days after the notice.

headings.title: Disputing penalties, arbitration, and pre-enforcement back-wage payment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note (A.L. 2007 S.B. 339, A.L. 2018 H.B. 1729, et al.). Grants employers forty-five days to dispute a penalty notice in writing, establishes arbitration under department rules conforming to AAA guidelines or another mutually agreed process, and precludes department penalty enforcement if the employer pays determined back wages prior to an enforcement action.

headings.title: Penalty enforcement actions and department enforcement costs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note (A.L. 2007 S.B. 339, A.L. 2018 H.B. 1729, et al.). Authorizes department enforcement of subsection 1 penalties if the employer fails to pay arbitrator-determined wages within forty-five days or fails to seek arbitration, and allows recovery of actual enforcement costs from court-ordered penalties.

headings.title: Preservation of aggrieved employee enforcement actions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note (A.L. 2007 S.B. 339, A.L. 2018 H.B. 1729, et al.). Clarifies that section 290.250 does not preclude an aggrieved employee's enforcement action as otherwise provided in law.

headings.title: Wage data submissions and weighted average prevailing wage
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, subdivisions (1)–(2)(b)a–b, and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1729, et al.). headings.title: Annual calculation of public works contracting minimum wage
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1729, et al.). Directs annual department calculation of each locality's public works contracting minimum wage at 120 percent of the locality average hourly wage determined by MERIC within the department of economic development or a successor agency.

headings.title: Annual initial and final wage order schedules
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1729, et al.). headings.title: One-thousand-hour threshold between prevailing and contracting minimum wage

headings.title: Meaning of reportable hours
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1729, et al.). Defines 'reportable hours' for section 290.257 as hours reported by a contractor for work performed under that contractor in a particular occupational title within a locality.

headings.title: Heavy and highway prevailing wage investigations and determinations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1957 p. 574 § 8, A.L. 1965 p. 95, A.L. 1969 S.B. 142, A.L. 2013 H.B. 34; 1962 United Bro. of Carpenters judicial review annotation). Covers periodic heavy and highway prevailing wage investigations, paper/electronic rate submissions, annual July 1 general wage orders for the highways and transportation commission, and consideration of CBA and locality rates.

headings.title: Filing determinations and supplying requested copies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1957 p. 574 § 8, as amended through A.L. 2013 H.B. 34). Requires immediate filing of certified copies of determinations with the secretary of state and department in Jefferson City, and supplying requested copies within ten days after filing.

headings.title: Written objections to heavy and highway determinations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and source notes (L. 1957 p. 574 § 8, as amended through A.L. 2013 H.B. 34). Allows any affected person to file a written objection stating specific grounds with the department within thirty days after certified copies are filed.

headings.title: Scheduling and notice of objection hearings
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and source notes (L. 1957 p. 574 § 8, as amended through A.L. 2013 H.B. 34). Requires the department to set a hearing date within thirty days of receiving an objection, hold the hearing within sixty days of receipt, and give objectors written notice at least ten days beforehand.

headings.title: Consolidation of objections and hearing evidence
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and source notes (L. 1957 p. 574 § 8, as amended through A.L. 2013 H.B. 34). Authorizes separate or consolidated hearings on written objections, requires the department to first introduce its original investigation and facts, and permits material evidence from the department, objector, or any interested party.

headings.title: Final rulings, filing, and service on parties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and source notes (L. 1957 p. 574 § 8, as amended through A.L. 2013 H.B. 34). Requires a final determination within twenty days after hearing conclusion, immediate certified filing with the secretary of state and department, and service on all parties personally or by registered mail.

headings.title: Judicial review under chapter 536 and constructive service
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and source notes (including 1962 United Bro. of Carpenters v. Industrial Commission annotation on competent and substantial evidence review). Subjects final prevailing wage decisions to chapter 536 review by any affected person regardless of administrative participation, treating secretary of state filing as service on nonparticipants.

headings.title: Intervention in chapter 536 review proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and source notes (L. 1957 p. 574 § 8, as amended through A.L. 2013 H.B. 34). Permits any affected person to intervene before trial in chapter 536 review proceedings and become a party.

headings.title: Court docket priority for wage determination proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and source notes (L. 1957 p. 574 § 8, as amended through A.L. 2013 H.B. 34). Gives court proceedings affecting department determinations under §§ 290.210 to 290.340 priority in hearing and determination over all other pending civil proceedings except election contests.

headings.title: Annual cost-of-living adjustments from 2008 through 2024
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (amended through A.L. 2024 Prop A and A.L. 2025 H.B. 567, et al.). Provides annual January 1 CPI-W cost-of-living adjustments from January 1, 2008, through December 31, 2024, measured each September 30 over prior-July levels and rounded to the nearest five cents.

headings.title: Minimum wage schedule for 2025–2026 and federal floor
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note (amended through A.L. 2024 Prop A and A.L. 2025 H.B. 567, et al.). Notwithstanding subsection 1 and subject to §§ 290.500 to 290.530, sets a $13.75 minimum wage effective January 1, 2025, increasing by $1.25 to $15.00 effective January 1, 2026, with immediate adoption of any higher federal minimum wage rate.

headings.title: Definition of public employer and August 2025 coverage
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note (amended through A.L. 2024 Prop A and A.L. 2025 H.B. 567, et al.). Defines 'public employer' for section 290.502 and applies the section to public employers with respect to their employees beginning August 28, 2025.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 290.502:57193, all four subsections, and history note (L. 1990 H.B. 1881 § 2, A.L. 2006 Prop B, A.L. 2018 Prop B, A.L. 2024 Prop A, A.L. 2025 H.B. 567, et al.); verified sourceUrl, sourceSha256, textSha256, and every subsection bodySha256. Checked multi-era minimum-wage structure: Jan. 1, 2007 $6.50/federal floor rate, Jan. 1, 2008 through Dec. 31, 2024 CPI-W adjustments, Jan. 1, 2025 ($13.75) and Jan. 1, 2026 ($15.00) schedule with immediate higher-federal-rate adoption, and public employer definition with Aug. 28, 2025 coverage start. Revised subsection 3 to include the immediate higher-federal-rate floor alongside the 2025–2026 schedule; retained subsections 1, 2, and 4.

headings.title: General overtime rate over forty hours
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1990 H.B. 1881 § 3, A.L. 2006 Prop B, A.L. 2008 H.B. 1883 merged with H.B. 2041; dual effective dates 6-25-08 for H.B. 2041 and 8-28-08 for H.B. 1883). Requires one-and-one-half times regular pay for workweek hours exceeding forty, subject to section 290.505 exceptions.

headings.title: Overtime threshold for certain amusement or recreation businesses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes (dual effective dates 6-25-08 for H.B. 2041 and 8-28-08 for H.B. 1883). Requires one-and-one-half times regular compensation for hours over fifty-two per week for employees of amusement or recreation businesses meeting 29 U.S.C. 213(a)(3) criteria.

headings.title: Exclusion of federally exempt employees except subsection 2
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and source notes (dual effective dates 6-25-08 and 8-28-08). Exempts employees exempt from federal minimum wage or overtime requirements (including 29 U.S.C. §§ 207 and 213 exemptions/formulas and regulations) from subsection 1 overtime requirements, except for subsection 2 employees (retaining verbatim parenthetical references 'subsection (2)' and 'subsection (1)').

headings.title: Interpretation in accordance with federal labor statutes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and source notes (dual effective dates 6-25-08 and 8-28-08). Directs interpretation of section 290.505 in accordance with the Fair Labor Standards Act (29 U.S.C. § 201 et seq.), the Portal to Portal Act (29 U.S.C. § 251 et seq.), and related regulations, except as otherwise provided under §§ 290.500 to 290.530.

headings.title: Minimum wage calculation for tipped employees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1990 H.B. 1881 § 6, A.L. 2006 Prop B). Limits required direct wages for employees receiving and retaining gratuities to fifty percent of the §§ 290.500 to 290.530 minimum wage, provided total compensation equals at least the minimum wage with the employer making up any difference.

headings.title: Non-discretionary goods or services credit and valuation rules
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1990 H.B. 1881 § 6, A.L. 2006 Prop B). Reduces required employer cash wages by the weekly fair market value of non-discretionary goods or services received and retained as an incident of employment, and directs the director to establish valuation and eligibility methods by regulation.

headings.title: Definitions for local wage and benefit limitations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, subdivisions (1)–(4), and history note (L. 1990 H.B. 1881 § 13, A.L. 2006 Prop B, A.L. 2017 H.B. 1194 & 1193). Defines 'employee', 'employer' (excluding any public employer defined in § 285.525), 'employment benefits', and 'political subdivision' for section 290.528.

headings.title: Preemption of local wage and benefit mandates exceeding state law
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2, subdivisions (1)–(2) plus continuation div block, and history note (L. 1990 H.B. 1881 § 13, A.L. 2006 Prop B, A.L. 2017 H.B. 1194 & 1193). Prohibits political subdivisions from requiring employers to provide minimum or living wages or employment benefits exceeding state laws, rules, or regulations, and states that §§ 290.500 to 290.530 preempt and nullify existing or later-enacted local ordinances, rules, and regulations doing so.
